title: Corn, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen corn cooked with butter or margarine is a ready‑to‑eat side dish made from mature corn kernels that are cleaned, blanched, flash‑frozen and then quickly sautéed or boiled in butter or margarine. The result is a tender, buttery‑flavored vegetable.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn is one of the world’s most widely consumed grains.
Freezing preserves most B‑vitamins and carotenoids that give the kernels their yellow hue.
Cooking with butter or margarine boosts the content of fat‑soluble vitamins A and E.
Corn contains the eye‑protective antioxidant lutein.
In the United States frozen corn is a common accompaniment to barbecues and steaks.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Corn provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Fresh corn contains vitamin C, which is partially retained after freezing and cooking.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin help protect the eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbohydrate
items.content: Starch offers a quick source of energy, while added fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble nutrients.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Corn supplies magnesium, potassium and iron, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small percentage of people may experience allergic reactions to corn.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared versions are often salted; individuals with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Trans‑fat presence
items.content: If margarine is used, it may contain trans fats, which should be limited.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Added butter increases calories; servings should fit within daily energy needs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen corn in a skillet, microwave, or steamer, stirring until hot and lightly golden. Enhance with fresh herbs, spices, cheese, or a squeeze of lemon for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C. Once the package is opened, use within 3–4 months. Do not thaw and refreeze, as quality will deteriorate.
